bounds: Two notification sequence values, a serial write owner, append/read-mark/delete/clear actions, one atomic cache snapshot per agent, failures before or after commit, one stop/restart cycle at a time. The payload case follows one admitted notification, one producer, one reusable observer slot and two payload values.
fairness: AdmittedOperationSettles assumes weak fairness for each enabled local mutation, persistence acknowledgement, reconciliation read and observational broadcast. AdmittedPayloadPersists assumes weak fairness for materialization and a successful write. Permanent non-settling host/storage operations are excluded from progress.
limitations: A single serial owner is explicit. Concurrent independent NotificationService instances writing the same agent cache need a separate cross-process ownership model.

Hydration begins with a valid version-2 snapshot. Legacy migration and malformed coordinate rejection remain separately test-covered. NotificationGroupPolicy checks grouped replacement and retention. The full category-to-priority mapping remains outside these models.

The write-queue case projects title/body/data content to identity plus a read mark. The payload case represents complete nested JSON by a distinguishable value and checks its ownership independently of write ambiguity. The real SQLite case covers writes, live events, grouped callbacks, list APIs and restart.
Storage operations are atomic but their outcome may be ambiguous to the caller. Restart in this case assumes a successful read of the durable version-2 snapshot.
Ordinary synchronous list/getUnreadCount APIs can observe provisional in-memory work. The DurableFence invariant concerns the quiescent native and durable-read APIs.
Conformance executes 70 real SQLite/runtime tests. Named scenarios gate real API effects and do not establish exhaustive schedule equivalence.

assumptions: Checked formula in NotificationDurability: AdmittedOperationSettles = (mutate.weakFair(s) and exhausted.weakFair(s) and persist("ack").weakFair(s) and reconcile(true).weakFair(s) and broadcast(true).weakFair(s)).implies((s.phase != "idle").leadsTo(s.phase == "idle"))
The property is conditional on its written model fairness and environmental premises. Real scheduler fairness, provider completion and implementation refinement are not proved.
No fairness. Check the payload captured at submission and its stability in every later transition.
Assume weak fairness of materialize and persist. This case assumes that storage can complete a write. Ambiguous storage outcomes are covered by the durable-writes case.
No fairness. A submitted payload can wait indefinitely without materialization or persistence.
